headline: Centrica chief alarmed as UK energy bills set to jump
pages: The chief executive of British Gas owner Centrica says he is hugely concerned about the expected jump in UK energy bills in January. Chris O'Shea told the BBC more people will be unable or unwilling to pay once prices rise. The new price cap is announced Wednesday, and Cornwall Insight forecasts a rise of 443 pounds a year, or 26 percent, to 2,166 pounds for a typical household. 60 pounds a week to every electricity customer's cost. Households owed suppliers 5bn pounds in April to June, per Ofgem. The government plans 100 pounds of help for some households, which Citizens Advice called a drop in the ocean. Wholesale prices have risen with the Middle East conflict. Source: BBC News.
